title: Body-Centered Interaction in VR Narrative Storytelling: A Systematic Literature Review
content: Virtual reality narratives increasingly use bodily participation to shape how stories unfold and are experienced. This systematic review examines the narrative functions of bodily mechanisms and the theories and evidence used to explain them in VR and related spatially embodied AR/MR environments. Searches of Web of Science, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and ACM Digital Library identified 370 reports published between January 2015 and April 2026. Cinematic VR and 360-degree embodiment, avatar embodiment and perspective-taking, and locomotion were the primary foci in 219 of 367 RQ1 reports. Substantive theoretical use appeared in 340 reports, including 44 with explicit cross-family integration. Comparative or associational evidence appeared in 232 reports; 54 contributed methodological diagnoses only. Close comparison of 32 purposively selected reports examined how bodily configurations acquire narrative functions and how designed cues relate to participant interpretations. Body-Centered Narrative Coherence (BCNC) brings these relations into an analytical framework organized through bodily anchoring, theoretical congruence, and empirical traceability.
